memory_candidates.content: literature-chunk.sh writes chunks.json in mode 'w' (overwrite, no append). When a doc has multiple valid .md files that must share one doc_id (a multi-file book or a document split across chapter files), chunk each file into a DISTINCT subdirectory (e.g. sources/<dir>/.chunks/<name>/) all passing the same --doc-id; literature-build-index.sh --global/--local recursively discovers every chunks.json under the target dir and keys chunks by the in-manifest doc_id field, so distinct subdirs aggregate naturally without any chunker contract change or manifest-merge logic.

In the literature pipeline, .claude/skills/skill-literature/SKILL.md is a symlink to ../extensions/literature/skills/skill-literature/SKILL.md (not a separate copy). Editing the extension source automatically keeps the deployed path in sync -- `cp` + `diff -q` checks pass trivially. `git add`/`git status` on the symlinked deployed path errors with 'beyond a symbolic link'; stage only the extension source path in commits.

literature-search.sh's default ranked output excludes docs without a provenance_fidelity stamp (fail-open to 'unverified'), because that field is written by a separate literature-fidelity-audit.sh --write pass, not by handle_convert()/literature-ingest.sh at conversion/chunk time. A freshly chunked+indexed doc is immediately present in chunks_data and findable via `--include-unverified`, but invisible to default search until fidelity-audited. This is expected, pre-existing behavior, not a coverage bug.
